Define the term impulse.

questions.question:
2.3
A cricket ball of mass 150 g is thrown horizontally with an initial velocity of 15 m·s⁻¹. It is struck by a bat and moves in the opposite direction with a velocity of 30 m·s⁻¹. The contact time between the bat and the ball is 0.03 s.

Calculate the average net force acting on the ball.

(4)
questions.answer:
2.3

Take the direction of the initial velocity as positive.
pi = mvi = (0.15)(15) = 2.25 kg·m·s⁻¹
pf = mvf = (0.15)(−30) = −4.5 kg·m·s⁻¹

FnetΔt = Δp
FnetΔt = pf − pi
Fnet(0.03) = −4.5 − 2.25
Fnet(0.03) = −6.75
Fnet = −225 N
Fnet = 225 N in the direction opposite to the initial velocity

(4)

questions.question:
2.4
A 1200 kg car travelling at 20 m·s⁻¹ collides head-on with a 2000 kg truck travelling at 15 m·s⁻¹ in the opposite direction. After the collision, the car moves at 5 m·s⁻¹ in the opposite direction.

Calculate the magnitude and direction of the velocity of the truck after the collision.

(5)
questions.answer:
2.4

Take the direction of the car's initial velocity as positive.

Σpi = Σpf
m1v1i + m2v2i = m1v1f + m2v2f
(1200)(20) + (2000)(−15) = (1200)(−5) + (2000)v2f
24000 − 30000 = −6000 + 2000v2f
−6000 = −6000 + 2000v2f
0 = 2000v2f
v2f = 0 m·s⁻¹

The truck is stationary after the collision.

(5)

(2)
questions.answer:
3.1
Marking criteria:
If any of the underlined key words/phrases in the correct context is omitted, deduct 1 mark.

The total linear momentum of an isolated/closed system remains constant (is conserved).

OR

The total linear momentum before a collision is equal to the total linear momentum after the collision in an isolated/closed system.

A 0.2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 5 m onto a hard floor. It bounces back to a height of 3.2 m. The ball is in contact with the floor for 0.02 s.

3.2.1 Calculate the velocity with which the ball strikes the floor.

3.2.2 Calculate the velocity with which the ball leaves the floor.

3.2.3 Calculate the average net force exerted by the floor on the ball.

(9)
questions.answer:
3.2.1

DOWNWARDS AS POSITIVE:
vf² = vi² + 2aΔy
vf² = (0)² + 2(9.8)(5)
vf² = 98
vf = 9.90 m·s⁻¹ (downwards)

(3)

3.2.2

vf² = vi² + 2aΔy
0² = vi² + 2(−9.8)(3.2)
0 = vi² − 62.72
vi² = 62.72

(3)

3.2.3

Take upwards as positive.
vinitial = −9.90 m·s⁻¹

FnetΔt = mvf − mvi
Fnet(0.02) = (0.2)(7.92) − (0.2)(−9.90)
Fnet(0.02) = 1.584 + 1.98
Fnet(0.02) = 3.564

questions.question:
3.3
A 4 kg block moving at 6 m·s⁻¹ collides with a stationary 2 kg block. After the collision, the 4 kg block moves at 2 m·s⁻¹ in the same direction.

3.3.1 Calculate the velocity of the 2 kg block after the collision.

3.3.2 Determine whether the collision is elastic or inelastic. Show ALL calculations.

(7)
questions.answer:
3.3.1

Σpi = Σpf
m1v1i + m2v2i = m1v1f + m2v2f
(4)(6) + (2)(0) = (4)(2) + (2)v2f
24 = 8 + 2v2f
16 = 2v2f
v2f = 8 m·s⁻¹

(3)

3.3.2

Total Ek before:
Ek_i = ½m1v1i² + ½m2v2i²
Ek_i = ½(4)(6)² + 0
Ek_i = 72 J

Total Ek after:
Ek_f = ½m1v1f² + ½m2v2f²
Ek_f = ½(4)(2)² + ½(2)(8)²
Ek_f = 8 + 64
Ek_f = 72 J

Since Ek_i = Ek_f, the collision is elastic.

(4)

(7)

questions.question:
3.4
A 0.15 kg cricket ball is thrown horizontally with a certain initial velocity and is struck by a bat so that the ball moves in the opposite direction. The average net force acting on the ball is horizontal.

The experiment is repeated using the same ball. The average net force and the initial velocity of the ball are kept constant. The contact time between the bat and the ball is changed EACH time. The results obtained are shown in the graph below.

| Contact time Δt (s) | Final momentum pf (kg·m·s⁻¹) |
|---|---|
| 0.01 | 0 |
| 0.03 | 4.5 |

3.4.1 Calculate the average net force acting on the ball.

3.4.2 Calculate the magnitude of the initial velocity of the ball.

3.4.3 Redraw the graph in the ANSWER BOOK and label it as A. On the same set of axes, draw the graph that will be obtained when a ball with a bigger mass is used, without changing the initial velocity and average net force. Label this as B.

(9)
questions.answer:
3.4.1

Gradient = Fnet = Δpf / Δt
Fnet = (4.5 − 0) / (0.03 − 0.01)
Fnet = 4.5 / 0.02
Fnet = 225 N
Fnet = 225 N to the right / opposite to the original direction of the ball

(3)

3.4.2

FnetΔt = Δp
FnetΔt = pf − pi
FnetΔt = mvf − mvi
(225)(0.03) = 4.5 − (0.15)vi
6.75 = 4.5 − 0.15vi
0.15vi = 4.5 − 6.75
0.15vi = −2.25
vi = −15 m·s⁻¹
vi = 15 m·s⁻¹

(4)

3.4.3

Criteria for graph:
• Graph A: Straight line passing through (0.01; 0) and (0.03; 4.5).
• Graph B: Straight line with the same gradient (parallel to A) but with a smaller y-intercept (more negative) and passing through a point with a lower pf value at the same Δt.
• Correct labels A and B.

NOTE: If labels A and B not indicated: 0/2
Award full marks for solid lines with labels.

(2)

(9)

4.1.3 Calculate the average net force exerted by the ground on the ball.

(10)

vf² = (5)² + 2(9.8)(10)
vf² = 25 + 196
vf² = 221
vf = 14.87 m·s⁻¹ (downwards)

(3)

4.1.2

questions.question:
4.2
A 1500 kg car travelling east at 25 m·s⁻¹ collides with a 2500 kg truck travelling west at 15 m·s⁻¹. After the collision, the car moves west at 5 m·s⁻¹.

4.2.1 Calculate the velocity of the truck after the collision.

4.2.2 Determine whether the collision is elastic or inelastic. Show ALL calculations.

(8)
questions.answer:
4.2.1

Take east as positive.

Σpi = Σpf
m1v1i + m2v2i = m1v1f + m2v2f
(1500)(25) + (2500)(−15) = (1500)(−5) + (2500)v2f
37500 − 37500 = −7500 + 2500v2f
0 = −7500 + 2500v2f
2500v2f = 7500
v2f = 3 m·s⁻¹ (east)

(4)

4.2.2

Total Ek before:
Ek_i = ½m1v1i² + ½m2v2i²
Ek_i = ½(1500)(25)² + ½(2500)(15)²
Ek_i = 468750 + 281250
Ek_i = 750000 J

Total Ek after:
Ek_f = ½m1v1f² + ½m2v2f²
Ek_f = ½(1500)(5)² + ½(2500)(3)²
Ek_f = 18750 + 11250
Ek_f = 30000 J

Since Ek_i ≠ Ek_f (Ek_i > Ek_f), the collision is inelastic.

(4)

(8)

questions.question:
4.3
A 2 kg block moving at 8 m·s⁻¹ collides with a stationary 3 kg block. After the collision, the two blocks stick together and move as one unit.

4.3.1 Calculate the velocity of the combined blocks after the collision.

4.3.2 Calculate the loss in kinetic energy during the collision.

(6)
questions.answer:
4.3.1

Σpi = Σpf
m1v1i + m2v2i = (m1 + m2)vf
(2)(8) + (3)(0) = (2 + 3)vf
16 = 5vf
vf = 3.2 m·s⁻¹

(3)

4.3.2

Ek_i = ½m1v1i² + ½m2v2i²
Ek_i = ½(2)(8)² + 0
Ek_i = 64 J

Ek_f = ½(m1 + m2)vf²
Ek_f = ½(5)(3.2)²
Ek_f = ½(5)(10.24)
Ek_f = 25.6 J

Loss in Ek = Ek_i − Ek_f
Loss in Ek = 64 − 25.6
Loss in Ek = 38.4 J

(3)

(6)
